findings.title: A retained first leaf projection can accept stale installed content after another owner effect
findings.violatedProperty: Physical verification may be reused only while its material installed-content dependencies remain valid, within the same prepared resolution; known or uncertain install-affecting effects must invalidate before reliance.
findings.producerToConsumer: prepareInstalledProductModules physically checks install -> productSemanticsFromModules/loadProductSemantics saves the acquisition in a WeakMap keyed by the imported provider -> projectInstalledLeafSemantics removes that entry and creates a private boolean -> constructAdmittedLeafInvocationPort and its first verifyAuthority both consume true without a physical read -> the latter releases only its own closure -> invokeLeafOwnerBoundary can load/invoke a leaf.
counterexample: Acquire an exact admitted install and create a genuine first semantics projection P. P retains unchangedInstallPremise=true; no live unchanged-content relation is carried with it.

Before P authorizes its first leaf, perform an install-affecting owner effect through a distinct projection Q, or observe an ordinary trusted-desktop content change. A second load/project creates a separate closure; releasing Q does not alter P. A subsequent failed physical verifier also does not revoke P.

Construct P's first port, or invoke its first leaf if its port was already constructed. All immutable install/publication/binding and admitted implementation coordinates can remain equal. P.verifyInstalledContent still resolves true, so the physical mismatch is not refused at the previously existing check.

The real single-traversal composition has this gap without concurrent calls: a parent beginning with C.workflow obtains a different child port through forGraphFunction; HoG uses that child port; the child's leaf releases only its own premise; child return restores the original parent runtime/port. If the child effect changes or may affect the shared install, the parent's first later leaf still borrows its old observation.
findings.causalAssessment: Historical acquisition success is promoted to an unchanged-install assertion solely from acquisition.install === install. The provider is a shared module export, not a resolution identity; each projection then owns independent invalidation. The second-port WeakSet observes only reuse of the identical runtime, so it does not cover sibling/child projections. This is a source-established missing dependency/invalidation relation, independent of the OWN-01 fixture failure.

Later checks on the same released runtime still verify physically, and each new resolution still initially verifies. No claim of a cross-resolution content cache implementation.
